items.body: But those observing the Toronto Maple Leafs from afar aren’t so sure. items.title: Flames’ Wolf gets feet wet again to mixed results after Cooley injury
items.summary: A lower-body injury to Devin Cooley opened the door for Dustin Wolf to start his redemption tour with the Flames. As Eric Francis writes, the results were mixed.
items.body: EDMONTON — As awkward a position as Dustin Wolf has been thrust in the last few weeks, it threatened to get infinitely tougher Wednesday night in Edmonton. Relegated to the sidelines since Oct. 15, as Devin Cooley has taken the league and the internet by storm, Wolf’s first shot at rebuilding his game came 20 minutes into a provincial battle with the NHL’s most potent team. A lower-body injury to Cooley, suffered late in the first period when Colton Dach drove towards the net and collided into the Flames netminder, opened the door for Wolf to start his redemption tour. “In the room we were trying to pump up a little bit, and just tell him we're here for him,” said captain Mikael Backlund . “It's never easy for a goalie to come in mid-game, no matter score and situation, so I thought he battled again.” Being beaten on the first shot didn’t help, as a Mattias Ekholm shot off the draw found its way through traffic and sailed over Wolf’s shoulder to put the hosts up 2-0. Wolf’s next big test came minutes later with a calm glove save on the world’s most dangerous player, Connor McDavid, who walked in with an uncontested shot from the hash marks. He then made a nifty kick-save off a tricky point blast and later slid across to make a left-pad save on a Leon Draisaitl one-timer from the low slot. items.title: NHL roundup: Tuch scores twice as Capitals beat Flyers
items.body: WASHINGTON — Alex Tuch scored his eighth and ninth goals in his first season with Washington, the second into an empty net to help the Capitals seal a 5-2 victory over the Philadelphia Flyers on Wednesday night. Tuch arrived in a trade from Buffalo and signed an eight-year, $84-million contract extension in June. On Wednesday, he became only the second player in Capitals history to score at least nine goals in his first 11 games for the team, joining Dino Ciccarelli, who scored 12 times in his first 11 Caps appearances to close the 1988-89 season. Matvei Michkov scored his ninth goal of the season and fifth on the power play for Philadelphia, which lost its third straight after an overtime defeat to visiting Columbus on Tuesday night. Sean Couturier levelled it early in the second, and Joseph Woll made 25 stops for the Flyers. items.title: Oilers cruise past rebuilding Flames in tame Battle of Alberta
items.summary: In the end, the Edmonton Oilers’ dominant record says more than any expert ever could. And Wednesday’s win over Calgary looked very much like a contender versus a rebuild, writes Mark Spector.
items.body: EDMONTON — If you’re dissecting the Edmonton Oilers overall game, you can always find a hole or two. No different than any other team, there are good nights, bad nights, and a bunch that fall somewhere in between. In the end, the record says more than any expert ever could, and at 9-2-2 and coming off a 3-1-1 homestand, there are a lot of other teams that would love to have the issues that Edmonton has right now. With the plane gassed up for a three-game road trip through the New York area starting Saturday, the standings say Edmonton has the second most points in the National Hockey League through this opening month. Complain if you must, but a .769 points percentage under a new coach off the start of the season ain’t chopped liver, no matter how much you might want to nitpick. Wednesday’s 4-0 win over Calgary looked very much like a contender versus a rebuild. At least, no one who watched that game would mistake one team for the other. “We just didn’t like the Toronto game (on this homestand). Every other game was OK,” said captain Connor McDavid , whose two assists give him 8-28-36 on the season, and a point in all 13 games so far. “(They had) big wins against some good teams (Minnesota and Carolina) there early — it wasn’t necessarily pretty. I don’t like the Toronto game (7-2 loss), but we were a minute away from winning the other night (4-3 shootout loss to Detroit)… “So there was lots to like from the homestand. Lots to build on too, as we continue to try and be better day in and day out.” A Calgary team that had taken three of four games from Edmonton a season ago lugged a four-game winning streak up a snowy Highway 2, on the day winter arrived in Alberta with a snowy, icy hello. It definitely helps me a lot." The Ducks, despite having lost six of seven games (1-5-1), are benefitting from LaCombe's Olympic experience as he leads them into a game against the Buffalo Sabres, and Olympic teammate Tage Thompson , at Honda Center on Thursday (10 p.m. ET; Disney+, HULU, ESPN+, SN+). items.body: It's true. The season opened Sept. 29. It's Oct. 29. This already is our fifth Super 16 Power Rankings since the start of the season. There still is so much more season to play, including two more outdoor games, an All-Star Weekend, the trade deadline and the final push to the Stanley Cup Playoffs. Edmonton made it 3-0 on the power play just 55 seconds into the third with a nice display of passing as McDavid sent it to Kapanen for his fourth. items.body: Register Login Capitals Activate Logan Thompson; Reassign Mitch Gibson By Brennan McClain | at October 28, 2026 3:58 pm After returning as a regular to practice yesterday, the Washington Capitals will return their starting netminder to the active roster. According to beat reporter Sammi Silber , the Capitals activated netminder Logan Thompson from the injured reserve and assigned Mitch Gibson to the AHL’s Hershey Bears. Thompson has been on Washington’s injured reserve with a lower-body ailment since their October 20th matchup against the Los Angeles Kings. Fortunately, the Capitals had only one game in the past week, limiting Thompson’s absence. Despite beating the Buffalo Sabres on Saturday, Washington likely wasn’t confident in Charlie Lindgren as the starter moving forward. The Capitals’ defense bailed him out for much of the game, limiting the Sabres to 21 shots on net through 63:42. Still, Lindgren stopped only 15 of those attempts, leading to a disappointing .857 SV% on the night. Now the Capitals can return to a netminder who has been on cruise control since joining the organization ahead of the 2024-25 campaign. This season, Thompson has earned a 4-3-0 record in seven starts with a .901 SV% and 2.90 GAA, including 1.9 Goals Saved Above Average. Throughout the past two years, Thompson has managed a dominant 62-27-12 record with a .911 SV% and 2.46 GAA, including two fourth-place finishes in Vezina Trophy voting. Meanwhile, Gibson returns to AHL Hershey without debuting in the NHL. He’s gotten off to a subpar start this season, splitting his first two appearances with an .881 SV% and 3.50 GAA.

items.summary: In Oliver Moore’s 70th NHL game, the promising forward made an ill-advised pass in Chicago’s offensive zone that led to a tying goal for Montreal.
items.body: CHICAGO — In Oliver Moore 's 70th NHL game, the promising forward made an ill-advised pass in Chicago's offensive zone that led to a tying goal for Montreal. In Moore's 71st game, he was all over the ice in a big win for the Blackhawks. That's how it's going at the moment in Chicago, where the team's youngest players are still learning on the job. Moore was a healthy scratch for Sunday’s 3-2 loss to Florida, but he returned to the lineup Tuesday night and played quite well in a 2-1 victory over the Los Angeles Kings. “I didn’t expect anything less,” coach Jeff Blashill said. “He actually was playing good hockey. I felt it was a moment where him and our team needed to make sure we learn these lessons about not beating ourselves. But he’s played good hockey, so it’s not like he went through a stretch where he hadn’t been playing well. He stepped right back in and did a good job.” Moore, a first-round pick in the 2023 draft, is a key figure for Chicago as it tries to find the other side of years of rebuilding. The 21-year-old Minnesota native signed a $21.25 million, five-year contract in September. Losers of eight of their first 12 games, the Blackhawks are looking for more offence once again. They are averaging 2.17 goals, ranking No. 31 in the NHL going into Wednesday's action. They averaged just 2.56 goals last season. Moore has elite speed and athleticism, but he is still working on finishing his scoring opportunities. He has two goals and one assist in 11 games after he had five goals and 14 assists in 51 games all of last season. Facing Montreal on Friday, he tried to make a backhand pass from the corner to Ryan Greene in the middle. It was intercepted by Owen Beck, who started a rush that led to Jake Evans' tying score in the first period of the Canadiens' 4-1 win.

The Sharks originally selected the six-foot-three, left-shot center in the first round (No. 27 overall) of the 2022 NHL Draft. The Sharks also recalled defenseman Libor Hajek on Wednesday while placing forwards Igor Chernyshov and Alex Wennberg on injured reserve. Additionally, the club assigned defenseman Luca Cagnoni to the Barracuda. The Sharks have lost three consecutive games and finally chose to recall Bystedt the day after they fell 2-0 to the Buffalo Sabres on home ice. Through 13 games this season, the Sharks sit just outside the Western Conference playoff picture with a 6-6-1 record and 13 points. After being drafted by the Sharks in 2022, Bystedt spent the subsequent two seasons with his hometown Swedish Hockey League club Linköping HC. He scored 15 goals and 37 points in 92 games over his two full campaigns with Linköping before arriving in North America in 2024. Beyond his club play, Bystedt also represented his native Sweden internationally at the 2023 and 2024 IIHF World Junior Championships, collecting seven goals and 14 points in 14 games across the two tournaments. items.title: Despite ‘prohibitive’ price, Larkin trade to Canadiens remains possible
items.summary: Here’s Eric Engels with the latest on the Dylan Larkin-to-Montreal buzz. It’s not about to die down, with the Red Wings heavily scouting the Canadiens, who have the assets to get this trade done.
items.body: The price for Detroit’s Dylan Larkin, according to league sources, isn’t just exorbitant. “It should be,” said one Eastern Conference executive, granted anonymity to speak openly about another team’s business. “He’s been a No. 1 centre for almost all his time there, and that has its own price. But factor in his cap hit ($8.7M through 2031) in this landscape, and that’s worth a premium.” This conversation was playing out over text while the Canadiens were completing a win in Chicago under the watchful eyes of Red Wings assistant general manager Kris Draper, who’s surely been following them for no other reason than due diligence for a potential trade. He was there in Toronto for Game 1 between the Canadiens and Leafs, then in Montreal for Canadiens-Sharks Oct. 20, and once again in Chicago for Canadiens-Blackhawks last Friday. There were rumblings he was at the Heritage Classic in Winnipeg Sunday—though we didn’t see him there—but he was definitely at Enterprise Center for Canadiens-Blues Tuesday, and it’s not because he’s suddenly become a fan of either team. If all of this smacks as absurd to you because Larkin hasn’t officially listed Montreal as one of the cities he’s willing to waive his no-movement clause for, consider that there aren’t many—if any—teams on his list loaded with the type of assets the Canadiens have to offer for the player’s services. Still, that doesn’t mean they’re willing to meet the current price that’s been set for the 30-year-old’s services. “It’s not about to come down, either, with the Wings hanging around and winning games,” added our league executive, and he was right. After losing five of their first six—one in a shootout to Montreal and one in overtime to the New Jersey Devils—the Wings have won four of six for a respectable 5-4-3 record.

items.title: Where the NHL salary cap could soar to in the next three years
items.summary: The NHL’s salary cap is still going through a “smoothing” process as the league comes out of the pandemic-induced flat cap wanting to avoid a sudden jump. But as we get to the end of that process, how high could the upper limit climb? Frank Seravalli has the story.
items.body: At the very end of his Board of Governors’ media conference last month on the 101 st floor of 30 Hudson Yards in Manhattan, NHL commissioner Gary Bettman offered an unprompted forewarning on the future of hockey’s salary cap. “Somebody had asked about the cap going up,” Bettman jumped in. “Please keep in mind that the cap going up at the rate it’s going up, it’s still a function of recapturing where we’re supposed to be after years of a flat cap,” Bettman said. “That number continues to be [managed] as we try to create a smooth increase in cap and not drive everyone crazy by who happened to be a free agent in a year with a huge jump.” Bettman reminded that once the system recaptures it, which he estimated “it will take two more years give or take,” then the cap “will go up at the same rate as revenues grow.” Fortunately for Bettman and the NHL, revenue continues to climb at record rates. But that means the salary cap will require even more finessing to smooth out drastic increases – because the cap is being kept so artificially low this season that there is a pending explosion. According to projections run by Sportsnet , verified by multiple team, league and Players’ Association sources, the NHL’s salary cap ceiling could reach $150 million USD by 2029-30 – just three seasons from now. That is a whopping 44 per cent increase from this season’s ceiling of $104 million. The calculation is relatively simple and we can use crumbs of information from Bettman’s media availability. He said last month that this season’s projected revenue was “just north” of $8 billion, or $8 billion “and change” in “mixed currency” since the league’s teams earn revenue in American and Canadian dollars. items.title: Charlie Jacobs to take over from father as Bruins’ governor
items.summary: Charlie takes the reins from his dad, Jeremy, continuing the family legacy that spans over a half-century.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images A huge change in operations in New England. On Wednesday, the Boston Bruins announced that CEO Charlie Jacobs is going to take over as the team’s governor from his father, Jeremy M. Jacobs, who held the role for 51 years. Charlie will represent the club on the NHL’s Board of Governors. “It is a tremendous honor to step into the role as governor of the Boston Bruins,” the younger Jacobs said in a release. “Representing the team that has been part of my family for the past 51 years. I step into this role with the goal of continuing to build upon the incredible legacy and the impact that my dad has had on this franchise and the NHL over his five decades of leadership. Dad will continue to serve as my mentor and sounding board through this next era of the Bruins. I am looking forward to partnering with the NHL Board of Governors Chairman Ted Leonsis, Vice Chair Murray Edwards, our peers, and Commissioner Bettman on continuing to grow this beautiful game that we all love.” The move to promote Charlie comes as Jeremy is starting to move out of the spotlight. Last month, he stepped down as Chairman of the league’s board of governors, and Washington Capitals owner Ted Leonsis was unanimously voted in as the new chair. Charlie has been part of the organization since 2000, when he was named the Bruins’ alternate governor. He also serves as the CEO of Delaware North, a multinational food service and hospitality company, which has ownership shares of NESN, the Bruins’ local broadcaster.

items.body: In the midst of a prolonged losing streak, the Vancouver Canucks were in desperate need of some good vibes. With just one win in the month of October, it was getting understandably difficult for the Canucks to maintain some positivity about what they're building towards. And when Quinn Hughes and the Minnesota Wild handed the Canucks their 10th straight loss Sunday, morale was at an all-time low. But Tuesday night against the Anaheim Ducks, the Canucks clawed back from an early deficit, earning an impressive 6-5 victory to get finally back into the win column thanks to an overtime snipe from Filip Hronek and some late-game heroics from Jonathan Lekkerimaki. It was a win that took a fair bit of resilience from a dejected Vancouver squad. For much of the night in Southern California, the Canucks looked to be headed to a familiar fate. But goals from Brock Boeser and Jamie Oleksiak in the early goings of the third cut into the Ducks' lead, perfectly setting the stage for Lekkerimaki to score twice with the net empty to force overtime. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images New York Islanders defenseman Matthew Schaefer exceeded all expectations in his rookie campaign last season. Now, just a dozen games into his sophomore season, he’s done something we haven’t seen in over 20 years. In New York’s 4-3 shootout win over the Nashville Predators on Tuesday, Schaefer became the first player since the 2004-05 lockout to play all five minutes of overtime. Schaefer drew a tripping penalty on Predators forward Filip Forsberg 2 minutes and 17 seconds into the overtime period, giving him a chance to grab a breather during a stoppage in what is typically relentless 3-on-3 action. Of course, the Islanders kept Schaefer out there for the entirety of the proceeding 4-on-3 power play, and he stayed on for the remaining 43 seconds after the power play had ended to complete the full five minutes of OT. The 19-year-old blueliner even had to get on his horse to impede a potential breakaway for Forsberg after he stepped out of the penalty box. The Hamilton, Ontario native finished the game with 32 minutes and 16 seconds of ice time, clearing the next closest Islanders skater by over six minutes. Coming into Tuesday’s game, he was averaging 26 minutes and 13 seconds of ice time. Schaefer is the first player to not take a shift off in an overtime period since the NHL began tracking that data in 2009-10. He finished the game with 32:16 of ice time, the third most by any player in a game this season, and picked up an assist. The reigning Calder Trophy winner has once again anchored the Islanders through the first month of the season. He now has 11 points in 12 games while averaging 26:43 of ice time, fourth most league-wide. The assist extended his personal point streak to five games. Kyle Palmieri and Bo Horvat scored in the shootout as the Islanders salvaged a win after letting an early lead slip away. Horvat, Anthony Duclair and Brayden Schenn had staked the Islanders to a 3-0 lead in regulation but the Predators forced overtime with goals from Filip Forsberg, Alexander Kerfoot and Ryan O'Reilly. items.summary: Kent Johnson scored his second goal of the game 2:22 into overtime and the Columbus Blue Jackets beat the Philadelphia Flyers 4-3 on Tuesday night after coughing up a three-goal lead.
items.body: PHILADELPHIA — Kent Johnson scored his second goal of the game 2:22 into overtime and the Columbus Blue Jackets beat the Philadelphia Flyers 4-3 on Tuesday night after coughing up a three-goal lead. Columbus scored three goals in a 2:46 span of the first period to lead 3-0 after one. Johnson set up Adam Fantilli for the first goal at 10:58 of the first period, and then deflected Zach Werenski's shot past Flyers goalie Dan Vladar at 12:54. Denton Mateychuk scored for Columbus 50 seconds later. Cam Talbot made 28 saves for his third win this season. Johnson scored the overtime winner on a two-on-none breakaway, following a give-and-go with Fantilli. It was Johnson's sixth goal of the season. Philadelphia forced overtime by outshooting Columbus 28-6 over the final two periods. Noah Cates scored his first goal of the season by poking a loose puck past Talbot, while Trevor Zegras cut the deficit to 3-2 with just under five minutes left in regulation. Zegras slid a pass to Tyson Foerster, who fired a shot on Talbot that Jamie Drysdale tipped into the net with 11 seconds remaining. Despite losing consecutive games, the Flyers have scored points in four of five games after starting the season with a franchise-record nine-game winless streak. Columbus won consecutive games for the first time this season. Blue Jackets: Continue their road trip in Carolina on Thursday. Flyers: Travel to Washington to play the Capitals on Wednesday.

items.body: TEMPE, Ariz. — Dave Hakstol left his job as an NHL assistant coach during the season to lead a college hockey program still reeling from the collapse of a player during an outdoor workout. Mayich is still hospitalized and is unlikely to recover from external heat stroke that reduced the flow of oxygen to his brain. Arizona State brought in former Arizona Supreme Court Chief Justice Scott Bales to lead an independent review, requesting it be completed by early December. items.body: Center also played for Black Hawks, Whalers, with Canada in Summit Series Andre Lacroix , an original member of the Philadelphia Flyers and the leading scorer in World Hockey Association history, has died at the age of 81. Lacroix began his NHL career with the Flyers in 1967-68 and played 245 games with them over four seasons. The center led Philadelphia in points twice, finishing with 56 points (24 goals, 32 assists) in 75 games in 1968-69, and 58 points (22 goals, 36 assists) in 74 games in 1969-70. Lacroix then was traded to the Chicago Black Hawks for 1971-72 before joining the WHA with the Philadelphia Blazers the following season, when he led the league with 124 points (50 goals, 74 assists). He also played for the New York Golden Blades/Jersey Knights, San Diego Mariners, Houston Aeros and New England Whalers over his seven WHA seasons. In 1974-75, his first season with San Diego, Lacroix won his second WHA scoring title with 147 points (41 goals, 106 assists) in 78 games. He also set the professional record for assists that season; at the time, he was the only player other than Bobby Orr (102 assists for the Boston Bruins in 1970-71) who had ever reached 100 in a single season of professional hockey. The record stood until Wayne Gretzky had 109 assists for the Edmonton Oilers in 1980-81. Lacroix is the WHA all-time leader in points (798, including 251 goals), assists (547) and games played (551). Following the WHA-NHL merger in 1979, Lacroix returned to the NHL for a sixth and final season, playing for the Hartford Whalers in 1979-80 before retiring. He finished with 198 points (79 goals, 119 assists) in 325 NHL regular-season games and seven points (two goals, five assists) in 16 Stanley Cup Playoff games. Do head coach Jeff Blashill and GM Kyle Davidson have any legitimate solutions to fix this team? The Detroit Red Wings are a perfect example, as they once were the league’s gold standard, but for the past decade they've missed the Stanley Cup playoffs. In the same boat – under nearly identical circumstances as the Red Wings – are the Chicago Blackhawks . items.title: Golden Knights turn to Adin Hill after Carter Hart exits morning skate with injury
items.summary: Vegas Golden Knights goalie Carter Hart left the team’s morning skate with an undisclosed injury, and Adin Hill will start Tuesday night’s game against the Ottawa Senators.
items.body: LAS VEGAS — Vegas Golden Knights goalie Carter Hart left the team's morning skate with an undisclosed injury, and Adin Hill will start Tuesday night's game against the Ottawa Senators. “He's in good hands,” coach Ryan Craig said. “We've got a plan here moving forward either way. We'll be ready for tonight.” Hart is 4-3-1, with a 2.76 goals-against average and an .889 save percentage, but he has shared much of the net time with Hill (4-1, 2.95, .882). Both goaltenders have dealt with injuries over the past several seasons. Hart missed nearly three months last season after injuring his left leg and then was expected to back up Hill in the playoffs. But then-coach Bruce Cassidy was fired with eight games left, and replacement John Tortorella instead put Hart in the net. Hart delivered by helping lead a late surge in the regular season before going 12-4 over the first three rounds with a 2.22 GAA and .924 save percentage. He struggled in the Stanley Cup Final against Carolina, however, becoming the first goalie to allow at least four goals in the first five games. The Hurricanes won the series in six games. Hart's presence in Vegas was a controversial topic in the hockey world and beyond. He was one of five players from the 2018 Canada world junior team who were acquitted last July of sexual assault. The NHL ruled those players were eligible to sign deals beginning Oct. 15, 2025, and to play starting Dec. 1. Hart signed a two-year, $4 million contract with the Golden Knights.

items.body: Register Login Blue Jackets Activate Dante Fabbro By Brennan McClain | at October 27, 2026 2:31 pm According to a team announcement , the Columbus Blue Jackets activated defenseman Dante Fabbro from the injured reserve. Columbus had an open roster spot, so they didn’t need to make a corresponding roster move. Fabbro, 28, has been recovering from a broken hand suffered in preseason. The right-handed blueliner will return after missing the first four weeks of the regular season and the Blue Jackets’ first nine games of the 2026-27 campaign. Based on line rushes from practice, Fabbro will play on Columbus’ bottom pairing next to Erik Gudbranson . Fabbro will begin his ninth NHL season and second full season with the Blue Jackets. Columbus claimed Fabbro off waivers from the Nashville Predators around this time a few years ago. The early stages of his tenure with the Blue Jackets were promising. Fabbro typically played with Zach Werenski , allowing him to score nine goals and 26 points in 62 games with a +23 rating, averaging 21:39 of ice time per game. He also earned a 91.7% on-ice SV% at even strength, one of his career-best marks. Given his chemistry with Werenski, Columbus quickly signed Fabbro to a four-year, $16.5MM ($4.125MM AAV) extension. Unfortunately, he didn’t play as well last season. Fabbro finished the 2025-26 campaign with five goals and 11 points in 74 games with a -16 rating, averaging 16:34 of ice time per game. He continued to block shots at a high rate, but nearly every offensive and defensive metric fell. Regardless, the Blue Jackets continue to inch toward a healthy defensive corps. After activating Fabbro, defenseman Ivan Provorov is the only defenseman left on the injured reserve as he continues to recover from a lower-body injury.

items.title: Panthers coach Paul Maurice goes to bat for Jets after Hellebuyck saga
items.summary: Paul Maurice doesn’t think Winnipeg suddenly has become a bad place to play in the aftermath of the Connor Hellebuyck saga.
items.body: Paul Maurice doesn't think Winnipeg suddenly has become a bad place to play in the aftermath of the Connor Hellebuyck saga. The Florida Panthers coach, in the Manitoba capital to take on his former team, was asked about Hellebuyck's trade demand and eventual deal last week to the New Jersey Devils on Tuesday. "I know the guys that play for the Winnipeg Jets ; the guys in that room love playing here. That's been true," said Maurice, who coached the Jets from 2014 to 2021. "Take a look at a guy like (Jets captain) Adam Lowry. I think sometimes, unfortunately, we have to take notice of the players that leave, but probably like you did this weekend (at the Heritage Classic), celebrate some of the great Jets that have been here, and you've got some great ones in your room." Over the years, things haven't always ended well with prominent Jets players. However, guys like Hellebuyck, Mark Scheifele and Kyle Connor did sign extensions with the small-market franchise. Maurice has maintained a deep connection to Winnipeg, saying, "If I could have one more thing, it's for the Winnipeg Jets to win the Stanley Cup," in a Sportsnet television interview on the ice after the Panthers captured their first of back-to-back titles in 2023. He was Hellebuyck's coach in Winnipeg when the goaltender broke into the league in 2015. "I don't know if it's (players) repeatedly wanting out. It's true in every market; it's just very personal for you when it happens," Maurice said. "When you're on a roll, everybody loves it. If you're not on a roll, nobody loves it. items.title: Jack Roslovic playing his best for Maple Leafs, but later than he wished
items.summary: Jack Roslovic is riding the high of his best October yet, and it’s not particularly close.
items.body: SEATTLE — Jack Roslovic is riding the high of his best October yet, and it’s not particularly close. Prior to Monday’s loss in Calgary and Tuesday’s flight to Seattle, his team, the Toronto Maple Leafs , had just ripped off four consecutive regulation wins, outscoring the opposition 21-9. Three of those victims were all former teams of the winger, who has spent his career ping-ponging around lines and throughout the league. In a span of five days, Roslovic splashed the scoresheet against his old pals on the Rangers, Blue Jackets, and Oilers. Six points in three revenge games. A newly entrenched first-liner hopping the boards with one of his buddies and tripling down with money on the board. Yet when you approach the smiling 29-year-old in the Rogers Place visitors’ room Saturday night after a 7-2 thumping of the most recent organization that didn’t re-sign him, Roslovic tries to wave the microphones away. “Go talk to him,” Roslovic motions to goalie Anthony Stolarz. “He’s the star of the game.” “I mean, playing with a little edge. You know, a little something special for me,” Roslovic allows. “But at the end of the day, it’s still a game for our team and just liking that we're all playing the right way.” NHL life has never felt so right so swiftly for the Columbus native, who signed his first multi-year contract since 2022 with the Leafs this summer and has already piled 13 points through 14 games.
